correctness.rationale: For n>=4, double transitivity supplies every ordered (i,j). Reversing pairs separates intensity equations into constant squared-distance defect c=|a|²-|b|² and equal real mean-direction pairings. For centered configurations y,z in R², J double centering yields Gz-Gy=(c/2)J with PSD Gram matrices rank≤2. If c>0, rank Gz>=n-1>=3; if c<0, on a centered nullvector of Gy, Gz becomes negative, both contradictions. Equal Gram matrices give z_i=O y_i with some O in O(2), and the pairing identities and |a|=|b| permit O to map a to b even for one-dimensional or zero spans. O is rotation or rotated conjugation. All n>=4 follow analytically; the viewed Gaussian-integer 625-signal n=4 script is strictly bounded.
